packets.title: TypeScript: interface members are METHOD nodes (`method_signature`, and a `property_signature` whose type is a function type) recorded in `interface_methods`, so an interface-typed receiver binds its CALLS (A6.6) and implementations pair through method-level IMPLEMENTS
packets.rationale: Seed §D: 'TS interface members are not METHOD nodes, so interface-typed receivers bind nothing.' Re-verified at HEAD 37fb9384: `export interface Store { load(id: string): string; }` and `function run(s: Store) { s.load("x"); }` produce no edge from run. The machinery exists for other languages: graph/src/types.rs `symbols.interface_methods` (A6.6), graph/src/calls.rs reads it for an INTERFACE-typed receiver ('binds the interface's own METHOD through interface_methods (A6.6); the implementation is one method-level IMPLEMENTS hop further (emit_method_level_implements)'), and PHP / Go / Java mint interface METHODs. The TS parser's `visit_interface` (parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs) mints the INTERFACE only; class `method_signature` is deliberately ignored ('the implementation after it'), which is right for overload signatures in a class but leaves interfaces with no members.

packets.rationale: Seed §E W7 (DH.17b, beyond FD.15's IMPLEMENTS fix): 'an INTERFACE's FUNCTION children into module_symbols, with enclosing_package / bare_call_target treating an Elixir INTERFACE like a PACKAGE (then the parser's `BodyShape::is_contract` can drop `!self.children`); ... `import` / `use` keep their IMPORTS edge but bind no alias, and `alias X, as: Y` binds Y; LocalModuleIndex declares an INTERFACE's dotted prefixes like PACKAGE prefixes; StreamData `property` blocks as tests and ENDPOINTs for HTTP calls in test bodies.' W3 (DH.8): 'Absinthe `import_fields` is not expanded across modules' (HEAD graphql.rs says so). W5 (DH.12): 'elixir-grpc: a file only handed a channel (`GRPC.Channel`, no `GRPC.Stub`) gets nothing for a service without a Service / Svc suffix; the server side (`use GRPC.Server, service: ..`) mints no GRPC_SERVER.'
entry_points: graph/src/build.rs (build_elixir / ElixirModules / LocalModuleIndex) - the INTERFACE and alias rules
parsers/code/elixir/src/lib.rs - BodyShape::is_contract simplified; StreamData property blocks as test FUNCTIONs; `alias X, as: Y`

parsers/code/extractors/src/graphql.rs - Absinthe import_fields expanded across files through the object's module (a cross-file pass in the extractor's existing two-phase read, or a NavFact the graph expands: read graphql.rs's Absinthe path at the base and use whichever exists)

parsers/code/extractors/src/grpc.rs - `use GRPC.Server, service: X.Service` mints GRPC_SERVER for X; a channel-only client reads the stub module name from `X.Stub.m(channel, ..)` without the suffix rule

packets.title: EVM client residuals, TypeScript: hardhat-deploy `getContract('C')`, ethers `new ContractFactory(abi, bytecode, signer)`, waffle `deployContract(wallet, Artifact)`, a factory rebinding `const f2 = F.connect(s)`, inline `(await getContractFactory('C')).deploy()`, a factory passed to deployProxy, a spread config object (`{ ...escrowContract, functionName }`), viem encodeFunctionData / decodeFunctionResult / decodeEventLog, standalone web3-eth-contract, truffle's global `web3`, and the ABI join through DT.1q barrels and a local export list
packets.area: FD recall: EVM TS clients (seed §E W20 DT.10i, W21 DT.10d, W22 DT.10j, W23 DT.10g)
packets.rationale: Seed §E W21 (DT.10d): 'hardhat-deploy `ethers.getContract('C')`, plain ethers `new ContractFactory(abi, bytecode, signer)`, waffle `deployContract(wallet, Artifact)`, a factory rebinding `const f2 = F.connect(s)`, an inline `(await ethers.getContractFactory('C')).deploy()` and a factory passed inline to deployProxy mint no contract client.' W22 (DT.10j): 'a spread of a same-file config object ... counts dynamic; viem `encodeFunctionData` / `decodeFunctionResult` / `decodeEventLog`; the standalone `web3-eth-contract` `new Contract(abi, addr)`; truffle's global `web3` without an import.' W23 (DT.10g): 'the cross-file ABI join (engine/src/build/evm_abi.rs) does not follow TS re-export barrels ...; also unread: a local export list `const X = [..]; export { X }` (ExportLocal covers it) and tsconfig path aliases (TsAliasSet could be passed in).' W20 (DT.10i): 'an ethers class-field binding is read only inside its own class body (a subclass in another file calling `this.escrow.fn()` is not read); `R[name]` with a const-held name counts dynamic and is not folded through the const table'.

packets.title: Measured experiment (S4): the declaration-surface fingerprint, a commit-replay harness and a whole-update decomposition that size the body-only fast path per language on cohort repos; its report fixes which languages get a fast-path packet and in what order
packets.area: FA - incremental resolution (A: Stack Graphs-style partial paths + watch A2)
packets.rationale: Section A's Stack Graphs bet is 'one partial-path model across 20 languages is the unknown' (0.5.1 plan section 5), and R2-watch section 12 spike S4 is the open sizing question: 'replay the last ~200 commits ... count the share whose declaration surface is unchanged. Sizes A2's payoff.' R2-watch section 13 names single-language repos (one big group: glia's Rust, grpc-go's Go) as where only A2 helps. The task asks to start with the languages where it pays and justify the order, so this packet measures before any builder is touched. The model this release adopts (stated in the report, not literal github/stack-graphs, which is archived and would replace every builder with a per-language TSG DSL): per file a PARTIAL = its SURFACE (declarations: node ids / kinds / qnames / nav parents, imports with their rows, heritage refs, field / return types, method signatures, properties, the surface NavFacts) plus its BODY stubs (call sites, non-heritage refs, local types, body NavFacts, node cells); STITCHING = the builder's per-file resolution of the body stubs against the group's surface index (SymbolTable plus the language index: RustIndex, GoPackages, ...). A body-only edit leaves every other file's stitching valid.
packets.entry_points: as spec, but the report is dev-notes/surface-replay-0.5.6.md
packets.implementation:
1. engine/src/cache.rs: `pub enum Part { Surface, Body }` and `pub fn surface_class(f: &NavFact) -> Part`. Classification rule: a fact is Surface when ANOTHER file's resolution may read it (a builder or language hook looks it up by name across files), Body when only its own scope's resolution reads it. Read each variant's reader before classifying (grep the variant name in graph/src). Expected from the variant docs in code-domain/src/lib.rs (verify each): Surface - DeclaresFn, UsingNamespace, UsingName, FieldMount, InternalLinkage, ValueLiteral (read by const folds across files), AbstractMethod, UrlPrefixKey, TypeAlias, GoStringConst, GoPackageName, SliceResult, ReExportStar, ReExportNamespace, ReExportName, ExportLocal, Exports, EvmAbi, RiverpodProvider, Getter, Setter (`Const` / `Param` / `Field` are variants of the nested `Mount` enum MountArg / FieldMount carry, not NavFact variants: the match has the 27 NavFact arms); Body - MountArg (Go mounts re-key ROUTEs through RESOLVED calls: also flag it as a cross-file body dependency, below), ClientHost, ClientBase, MemberRead, MemberWrite, ReceiverType. Doc each arm in one line. 2. `surface_fingerprint(fp)`: serialize, in this order, through the same HashWriter / bincode streaming parse_fingerprint uses: (a) nodes as (id, kind, qname) sorted by id - NOT their cells (POSITION / CODE move on any edit); (b) nav.name_by_id, qname_by_id, kind_by_id, parent_of, children_of, field_types, return_types, method_sigs (by_id / by_name ordered, exactly as CanonicalNav does), and the local_types entries of MODULE scopes only (module-level / package-level variables: an importer's or another package file's receiver typing reads them, e.g. Go package vars through GoPackages, a Python module-level `x = Foo()` imported by name), in every language; (c) properties sorted; (d) imports with their rows (an IMPORTS edge's EVIDENCE line is the import row, so a moved import is a surface change); (e) refs whose category is INHERITS_FROM or IMPLEMENTS (heritage: resolution follows heritage edges), with rows; (f) nav_facts restricted to surface_class == Surface, per scope in id order, each scope's list in parser order. `None` when serialization fails. Also `pub fn surface_fingerprint_strict(fp)` = the same plus every node's POSITION cell payload (the declaration rows): the report measures both, because a fast path that cannot re-derive line-carrying outputs would need the strict one. 3. engine/examples/surface_replay.rs: args --repo, --commits N (default 200), --rev (default HEAD), --out. For each of the last N first-parent commits (`git rev-list --first-parent -n N `; std::process::Command in an example only, never in a build), for each modified (not added / deleted / renamed: `git diff --name-status ^ `, status M) file with a source language (`glia_engine::cache::surface_language`, a new pub fn in cache.rs delegating to the pub(crate) `crate::extract::detect_language`, which an example cannot call), read both blobs (`git show ^:

` / `:

`), parse each with `glia_engine::parse_one` (the flat extract API), compute surface_fingerprint and surface_fingerprint_strict, and record (commit, path, lang, loose_equal, strict_equal, has_body_cross_dep) where has_body_cross_dep = the file's parse holds a Body fact some OTHER file's resolution reads (MountArg today). Then time what a watch update spends on the group, through the public watch API (no hand-assembled builder inputs: build_rust needs the Cargo crates, the TS family its alias resolver): on a `git archive` copy of the repo at --rev in a temp dir, `glia_engine::watch::WatchSession::open`, then per language with edits 3 updates, each appending (then, next update, removing) one comment line in a file of that language (a body-only touch that rebuilds exactly its group); from each WatchUpdate whose `groups_rebuilt` is exactly that group, record phase_ms.language_build (group_ms), phase_ms.clone (clone_ms) and phase_ms.total (update_ms); medians of 3. Run with GLIA_THREADS=1 so group_ms is one group's sequential cost. 4. CONTROLS, run in the same replay: (i) null control: per commit up to 20 unmodified source files (same blob at ^ and ) are parsed twice and fingerprinted; any inequality is a fingerprint-stability failure and the whole run fails (no verdict is printed until it is fixed); (ii) positive control: every modified file whose diff adds or removes a line matching the language's top-level declaration pattern (def / class / fn / func / function / interface / struct / impl / trait / type at the file's top indent) must come out surface-changed; each violation is listed in the report and either explained (the declaration is nested in a body, so it IS body) or fixed in surface_class / surface_fingerprint before any verdict. 5a. Per (repo, language): edits, body_only_loose = share with loose_equal && !has_body_cross_dep, body_only_strict, group_ms, update_ms, build_share = group_ms / update_ms, projected_saving_ms = body_only_loose x group_ms (an UPPER bound: the fast path still stitches the edited files and re-fills the group's evidence). Print one `[surface-replay] repo= lang= edits= body_only=/ group_ms= update_ms= build_share= clone_ms= saving_ms= controls= verdict=` line per row and write --out JSON (rows sorted by repo, lang). 5. PASS RULE (stated in the report before the numbers): a language PASSES when, on at least one measured repo, edits >= 30, body_only_loose >= 0.40, group_ms >= 250 (release build), build_share >= 0.25 (the group build is a quarter of the update, so cutting it is visible end to end), and both controls hold. FA.24's rule (the clone cut) is read off the same rows: clone_ms >= 50 and clone_ms >= 0.20 x update_ms on at least one measured repo. Repos (public, with history; never ~/Code/webplatform, never a private repo): glia at its v0.5.2 tag (Rust), pop-os/shell (~/Code/shell, TypeScript), gorilla/websocket (~/Code/websocket, Go), and pallets/flask cloned fresh with full history into the scratchpad (Python; no local public Python repo has history). grpc-go at ~/Code/grpc-go is shallow (1 commit): `git fetch --unshallow` it if the network allows and add its row, else say so in the report. 6. dev-notes/surface-replay-0.5.4.md: the model (rationale's paragraph), the pass rules (fast path and FA.24's clone rule), the controls' results, the table (every row, both fingerprints), the verdicts and the ORDER of the language packets that pass: by projected_saving_ms descending, ties by language name. FA.3 (Python, the reference implementation of the per-file stitching seam) is built when Python passes OR any other language passes (it carries the seam the others reuse); FA.5 Rust, FA.6 TypeScript family and FA.7 Go each only on their own PASS. Aggregate numbers only (public repos). FA.24 (copy-free reuse of unchanged groups) is built only on its own clone rule's PASS.

packets.title: Canonical per-graph order: every RepoGraph's intra edges sorted by glia_core::canonical_edge_cmp and its unresolved_calls / unresolved_refs by a total key at the end of each group build (before the evidence fill), so a graph built in any emission order has one byte form
packets.area: FA - incremental resolution (A: Stack Graphs-style partial paths + watch A2)
packets.rationale: R2-watch section 5, A2 need (a): 'canonical intra-edge order in RepoGraph (today intra edges are emission-ordered; only cross edges get canonical_edge_cmp, merged.rs)'. A fast path that re-resolves one file's body appends that file's edges after everyone else's, so without a canonical order its graph could never be byte-identical to a clean build. MergedGraph::sort_cross_edges is the precedent (graph/src/merged.rs). unresolved_calls / unresolved_refs are persisted in the code section (store/src/code_section.rs `unresolved_calls` / `unresolved_refs`), so they need a total order too. FA.1's model: stitching = per-file resolution of body stubs against the group's surface index. build_python (graph/src/build.rs: merge_parses, build_symbol_table, resolve_imports_python, resolve_calls, resolve_refs, emit_method_level_implements) is the smallest builder and the reference for the seam the other languages reuse; Python is built first when FA.1's report passes Python or any other language (the seam is shared).
entry_points: graph/src/build/partial.rs (new; a child of build.rs, declared `mod partial;` beside `mod dart; mod go_wire;` in graph/src/build.rs, so no facade change) - `pub struct BodyEdit { pub parse: FileParse }`, `pub enum Refused { SurfaceMoved(String), Unsupported(&'static str), UnknownFile(String) }`, `pub struct RebodyStats { files, edges_removed, edges_added, calls_bound, refs_bound }`, `pub(crate) fn drop_file_outputs(g, file_nodes) -> FileOutputs` and `pub(crate) fn replace_file_nav(g, old_ids, new_parse)`

packets.implementation:
Model (doc it at the top of partial.rs): a file's PARTIAL is its surface plus its body stubs (FA.1's surface_class); the group's SURFACE INDEX is RepoGraph.symbols + nav's declaration maps; STITCHING resolves body stubs against it. A body-only edit = every edited file's engine::cache::surface_fingerprint is unchanged (the engine checks this before calling; the graph crate cannot see the engine, so rebuild_* re-checks the cheap invariant itself: the edit's node id set, kinds and qnames equal the graph's nodes owned by that file, else Refused::SurfaceMoved(path)).
1. File ownership: a node belongs to the file whose MODULE is its nav ancestor (walk parent_of to the MODULE; Python MODULE qname is the file's). `file_nodes(g, module_id) -> BTreeSet<NodeId>`.
2. Split build_python with NO behaviour change for a clean build: python_surface = merge_parses + build_symbol_table + the BINDING half of resolve_imports_python (what it writes into SymbolTable.module_import_bindings and the same-stem picks); python_stitch(files) = for the given files, in parse order: the IMPORTS-edge half of resolve_imports_python for their imports, resolve_calls over their calls, resolve_refs over their refs, emit_method_level_implements restricted to their classes. A clean build_python = surface then stitch(all files). If resolve_imports_python cannot be split without changing which bindings exist (a binding that depends on edges emitted earlier), keep it whole in the surface and note it; IMPORTS edges then carry rows that are in the surface fingerprint anyway (FA.1 step 2d). The evidence tally (`[evidence-graph]`) is summed over the stitch calls.
3. rebuild_python_bodies(g, edits): for each edit (sorted by its MODULE qname): (a) owned = file_nodes; (b) drop_file_outputs: remove every edge whose `from` is in owned, every unresolved_calls entry whose `from` is in owned, every unresolved_refs entry whose `from_module` is the file's MODULE; (c) replace each owned node's cells with the edit parse's node cells (same ids by the surface check), and the file's parse edges (fp.edges) are pushed again; (d) replace_file_nav: local_types and nav_facts entries of the owned scopes with the parse's; (e) python_stitch(g, the edit's imports / calls / refs / classes); then g.canonicalize() (FA.2). Duplicate-NodeId cells (merge_parses appends cells when two parses declare one id) are a Refused::Unsupported("shared node") case: detect them (an owned node whose id appears in another file's nav) and refuse.
4. Nothing else in g may depend on the edited file's body: Python's builder reads no body fact across files (verify by reading resolve_calls' receiver path: it reads the CALLER's own local_types and field_types / return_types, which are surface). Document the verification in partial.rs.
5. Unit tests in partial.rs (cfg(test), fixtures as inline parses through glia_parser_python's parse fn, which glia-graph has as a dev-dependency): for 6 edits (a call added, a call removed, a call moved down 3 lines, a body line inserted above two defs, a decorator-free method body change, an edit in a file that others import) assert `rebuild_python_bodies(build_python(old_parses), edits)` == `build_python(new_parses)` after canonicalize, compared field by field (nodes, edges, unresolved lists, properties; nav maps compared as sorted vecs); and a surface change (a def added) returns Refused::SurfaceMoved.

packets.title: Multi-repo WatchSession: `WatchSession::open_many(roots, opts)` builds the repos exactly as generate_many does (one walk per repo, identities disambiguated, the proto service set unioned, one joint pass tail) and `apply` routes each changed path to the repo whose root holds it
packets.rationale: 0.5.2 plan Q13 / section 3: multi-repo `glia watch --with` is 0.5.4's. R2-watch question 3: 'The proto service set is build-wide (mod.rs), so it touches every repo.' engine/src/build/mod.rs `assemble_many_with` is the composition to reproduce: phase 1 walks every repo and unions the RpcContext, disambiguates identities (`disambiguate`), phase 2 builds each against the union; `finish_build` runs the passes once over all graphs in argument order. Every update's graph must equal a clean generate_many of the same trees.
entry_points: engine/src/watch.rs - `pub fn open_many(roots: &[String], opts: &BuildOptions) -> Result<WatchSession, String>` (open(root) becomes open_many(&[root])); `pub fn roots(&self) -> Vec<&str>`

packets.implementation:
1. open_many: for each root (argument order): plan_walk + read_walk (with stat stamps) as open does, repo_identity; then disambiguate the identities against each other with assemble_many_with's rule (canonical_display of each root); one RpcContext from every repo's files (rpc.add_files in argument order); Setup per repo (overlay text: never - the session reads each root's own .glia/overlay.toml, as a multi-repo build does for slots > 0; slot 0 too since watch has no overlay_text); build: per repo the DC.2 stages (parse_and_graft with the repo's cache and the SHARED rpc, plan / fingerprint / reuse / build / fold groups, repo_markers, aux_graphs) appended in argument order, fills aligned, then ONE finish_build(graphs, fills, inputs (one RepoInputs per repo, argument order), opts, repos.len(), started); GenerateResult.repo_labels = arch::repo_label_map over (RepoId, root) pairs, repo_roots first-wins, parse_errors concatenated in argument order - exactly assemble_many_with's.
2. A root that is not a directory: Err (unlike generate_many, which keeps going: a watch needs every repo; doc it). Nested roots (one root inside another, after canonicalisation) are refused: Err `nested watch roots: <inner> is inside <outer>` - a clean generate_many reads the inner repo's files in BOTH walks, which a path router cannot reproduce. `save_cache` saves every repo's ParseCache to its own root (single repo: unchanged), so the CLI and pyo3 persist every cache through it.
3. apply(changed): each path goes to the one repo whose abs_roots hold it (roots never nest: step 2); paths under no root count `outside`. Each repo with named paths re-reads / re-plans as today (High durability is per repo). Then: services_fp = fp of the union over every repo's files; a union change is a full_rebuild reason `proto_services` for every repo's groups (their fingerprints include it). Repos with no named path are not re-read, but parse_and_graft still runs for every repo (their ParseCache entries, DC.4 memos and cached group builds make an untouched repo a cache hit throughout), so the joint graph is assembled from fresh stage outputs in argument order, exactly as a clean generate_many composes them. Scoped delta: the scope sides are the union of each repo's rebuilt groups' graph indexes offset by the repo's first graph index in the joint result.
4. Identity: a High `identity` path in one repo re-reads its identity and re-runs disambiguate over all repos; if any RepoId changed, every repo's cache context is revalidated (validate_context clears it) and the update is a full_rebuild `identity`.
5. EA.7's RankCache: built from the joint result's repo_roots / repo_labels, replaced after a changed update as today.
6. Markers: `[watch] open repos=<n> repo=<label1,label2,..> files=<n> groups=<g> nodes=<N> edges=<E> took=<ms>` (open of one repo keeps its old text: `repos=` is printed only when n > 1); the update line's `repo=` lists the repos that had named paths.
7. Unit tests in watch.rs (temp dirs): open_many over two tiny repos equals generate_many_opts of the same roots node-for-node (persisted bytes); a path in repo 2 rebuilds only repo 2's groups (`groups_rebuilt` keys carry the repo label prefix `<label>:<key>` when n > 1 - doc it); open_many over nested roots is an Err naming both; save_cache writes each repo's parse_cache.bin.

packets.implementation:
1. Fixture: repo A (server): `proto/greeter.proto` (service Greeter, rpc Hi), a Go server implementing it, a Go HTTP handler `GET /api/orders`, `go.mod` module `example.com/server`; repo B (client): a Go gRPC client calling GreeterClient.Hi, a TS fetch of `/api/orders`, and a `go.mod` requiring `example.com/server`, so the manifest_name / package_name identity classes form across repos.
2. After open_many([A, B]) and after every update: persist the session's layout to a temp dir and compare its bytes (every file) with `generate_many_opts([A, B], false, &opts)` + persist_result to another temp dir; also compare GenerateResult.parse_errors. Use the helper watch_parity.rs uses for single repos (layout byte comparison).
3. Scripted sequences: (a) body edit in B's client; (b) add an rpc to the .proto in A (B's needles must move: full_rebuild `proto_services`); (c) edit A's HTTP route path (cross-repo HTTP_CALLS edge removed / re-added); (d) edit B's go.mod require (High in B only); (e) add then delete a file in A; (f) a two-repo update (paths in both); (g) an .glia/overlay.toml added to B.
4. Random: 3 seeds x 15 ops over the op table {body edit A/B, decl edit A/B, add / remove file A/B, proto edit, go.mod touch, noop touch}, each op's expected group set computed by an oracle like watch_parity's `group_of`; assert byte identity after each op and that groups_rebuilt is a superset of the oracle's set.
5. Mark the slow random test #[ignore] only if it exceeds 60 s debug; otherwise it runs in the default suite.

packets.rationale: Section F item 3 (James 2026-10-16: 'yep add it'): 'Measure RSS over repeated applies on the 0.5.2 WatchSession, then cap or evict, with a [watch] RSS marker and a gate.' Data: it levels off (100 updates on glia: first 562 MB, plateau 615-685 MB, debug); repo-graph-8d measured a held session at 940 MB vs 500 MB for a rebuild loop on glia. 'The budget question is the plateau's size, not a leak.' What a session holds beyond one graph (R2-watch section 13: about 3x one graph): every group's cached pre-pass LangBuild (CachedGroup, engine/src/watch.rs), the ParseCache entries and DC.4 BuildMemo (engine/src/build/memo.rs), the result. The cached groups and memos are pure caches (a hit replays exactly what a miss computes), so evicting them changes time, never bytes. ALREADY SHIPPED, not respecced: memo entries of paths no longer walked are dropped (BuildMemo::retain, DC.4) and the CLI prints the RSS series (`[watch] emitted ... rss_mb=`, DC.8).

packets.rationale: §B 'When embeds run (James: we could have a way to determine when to run the embeds) ... Candidates for the spec run: glia watch embeds changed nodes in the background after an apply, debounced; install-hooks adds a post-commit / post-merge glia embed; a semantic query ... embeds them inline under a small threshold ... an explicit glia embed always works. A [embed] marker reports embedded / cached / stale counts.' Decision here: all four, each opt-in except the explicit command and the inline threshold (FB.7a, 64 nodes, writes nothing). Watch runs the embed on its own loop thread after the update is emitted, so it never overlaps a build's rayon pool (Engram's thrash finding); FB.3 makes the sidecar Low durability so the write does not re-plan the watch. The sidecar ships whatever FB.6 says (item 13: 'otherwise glia embed ships as a sidecar'), so this packet is not gated.

packets.rationale: §F item 14: 'The rankings can only name existing files: 128 of 222 files of the law-driven change were new; co-change is cold for 33-49% of seeds. Score, on held-out commits that add files, the directory a new file lands in and the sibling it was patterned on (structure, co-change, intent, calibration as in 0.5.3), against controls. If a ranker beats them on the gate repos, it ships as an answer in a follow-up wave of this leap; if not, the report closes it.'
entry_points: engine/examples/rank_eval.rs: `--place on`, `--place-md <file>`: the added-file query set, directory and sibling truths, the place rankers and controls
dev-notes/place-eval-<date>.md (new): the report
packets.implementation:
1. Query set: rank_eval's leak-free test commits (eligibility unchanged) that ADD at least one candidate-extension file (`git log --name-status --no-renames` A rows; renames are not additions); seeds = the commit's MODIFIED candidate files (k1 / k2 / half shapes over them; a commit with no modified file uses the find shape: intent text only); intent = the subject. Truth: DIR = the directories of the added files; SIB = per added file, the file of the parent revision with the highest line-set Jaccard to the new file's content (trimmed non-empty lines, `git show`), ties to the same directory then path; no sibling when the best Jaccard < 0.2 (counted).
2. Directory rankers, each a score per directory of the parent revision's candidate files, where a file's score counts toward its IMMEDIATE directory only (summing every level to the root would put the root and `src/` above every leaf by construction, so hit@k would measure depth, not placement); a truth file whose directory did not exist in the parent revision is scored on its nearest existing ancestor and the query is counted `new_dir` (reported separately, and in the pooled numbers): Dstr = sum of P1 / PT* file scores (rank_eval run_query) per directory; Dco = sum of C0 per directory; Dtxt = sum of T1s per directory; Dmm = mm-blend of the three (rank_eval's minmax helper); Dsel = the online pick among {Dstr, Dco, Dtxt, Dmm} by r3_select's prequential rule (EC.3's replay logic). Controls: Cseed = the seeds' directories by seed count, then depth desc; Cpop = directories by candidate file count; Crand = a seeded random order. Sibling rankers: the top-3 directories' files ordered by the same scores, plus control Csib = the most recently modified file in the seeds' directory.
3. Metrics: dir hit@1 / hit@3 (any truth directory in the top k, exact match on the immediate directory, the `new_dir` ancestor rule above), sibling recall@5, per (repo, shape), with the commit-cluster bootstrap CI of each ranker minus the best control (Cseed unless Cpop is better on that repo).
4. PASS rule (in the report before the numbers): the directory answer PASSES when one non-control ranker R (the same R on every repo) beats the best control on dir hit@3 with CI > 0 on at least 3 of the 4 public gate repos (glia's pinned v0.5.2 snapshot, pop-os/shell, gorilla/websocket, flutter/samples) and is not significantly below it on any; the sibling answer PASSES under the same rule on sibling recall@5 against Csib. A repo with < 30 added-file queries is `thin` (neither). The verdict line: `Placement: PASS (<ranker>[, sibling])` / `Placement: FAIL (<reason>)`.
5. The report dev-notes/place-eval-<date>.md: rule, coverage (queries with additions / all), tables, verdict; the four public gate repos only (the rank gate's public rule: no `--private` run feeds the report).

packets.implementation: 1. Inference (TS family only): a direct HTTP wrapper candidate (FH.4b step 1-3: a client call whose path is the owner's parameter) whose owner is a METHOD of a CLASS C and whose name is an HTTP verb (today dropped by the verb-name precision rule) or ambiguous only because several classes define it, becomes a heritage wrapper keyed (C's name, C's file, verb). Its `path_arg`, prefix / suffix and method are the FH.4b reading. A non-verb-named METHOD wrapper (`request(path)`) joins too when it is called as `this.request(..)`. 2. Classes: from each TS-family FileParse, every CLASS with its line span and its heritage (`extends` UnresolvedRef base name, the INHERITS_FROM ref the parser already emits) and the file's import table (`import { APIService } from "../api.service"`). A class D reaches C when its `extends` name is C's name and either C is declared in D's file or D's file imports that name from a specifier whose last path segment (code extension dropped, `index` read as its directory) equals C's file stem; transitively through in-repo intermediates (`LiveService extends APIService`, then `X extends LiveService`), depth <= 4. Several same-named C copies (plane's three) are fine: each candidate C defines the verb as a wrapper of the same shape, else the site is `ambiguous_base` and mints nothing. 3. Sites: inside D's span, `this.<verb>(` and `super.<verb>(` calls (wrappers.rs' existing site reader: definitions and commented calls are not sites) where D (and every class between D and C) declares no member named <verb> (an override shadows the wrapper; it may itself be a wrapper). Each site is read with `read_http_site` (one literal path starting with `/` or `http(s)://`, every hole right after `/`) and minted exactly as an inferred-wrapper site: EVIDENCE emitter `pass:inferred_wrapper`, rule `heritage_wrapper_call`, Weak; a test-code site is ORIGIN test_fixture with `"test_site":true` (FH.17). 4. Marker: the `[http-wrappers]` line gains ` heritage=<classes> heritage_sites=<s> heritage_minted=<m> ambiguous_base=<a>` (printed when any is non-zero). Binding it needs a Bare USES ref that the graph crate resolves through import bindings' and 'Abstract method signatures (CH.1 visit_abstract_method) do not yet read their type names as type_ref USES. That path does not call record_callable.' entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs: the FH.20 type-position walk emits, for a type name that is a named (or default) import binding of the file and not shadowed by a type parameter or a local type, one Bare USES UnresolvedRef per (scope, name) at the lowest row, rule `type_ref`; `visit_abstract_method` runs the same signature walk `record_callable` does
graph/src/calls.rs (resolve_refs): the Bare USES ref binds through the file's import bindings (the DT.5g value_ref path), to an INTERFACE / CLASS / ENUM node only
packets.implementation:
1. Parser: in the type positions FH.20 already walks (signature parameter / return types, annotations, generic arguments, `as` types), a type identifier (or the head of `Ns.T` when Ns is a namespace import: skip) that the file imports by name (`import { Dto }`, `import { Dto as D }`, `import type { Dto }`, `import Dto from`) and that no type parameter or local type declaration of an enclosing scope shadows, queues one Bare USES UnresolvedRef from the scope holding it (dedup per (scope, imported name), lowest row), rule `type_ref`. An in-file alias keeps FH.20's direct edge. 2. Abstract members: `visit_abstract_method` (CH.1) reads its parameters' and return type's names through the same walk, so an abstract METHOD gets type_ref USES both to in-file aliases and (via step 1) to imported types. 3. Graph: the Bare USES ref resolves as DT.5g's value refs do (through import bindings, re-export barrels DT.1q, workspace packages FH.5, tsconfig / bundler aliases FH.16), then keeps the edge only if the target is an INTERFACE, CLASS or ENUM node (an imported function or const named in a type position is not a type ref); unbound refs count. EVIDENCE graph:refs rule `type_ref`, Strong when bound through a named import. 4. Marker: `[ts-types] .. type_refs= imported_refs= abstract_refs= file=

packets.title: The calibration replay's serial per-commit work spread across cores: IDR routes and BM25 text indexes for every test commit computed up front in parallel (ordered), PPR solves pooled across commits; bit-for-bit records
packets.rationale: Probe at HEAD 06012cc6: the release rank_eval (target/release/examples/rank_eval, built 2026-10-31 04:31 by the W27 close-out) run on the gate's glia snapshot alone with the gate's flags (`bash scripts/rank-gate.sh flags` COMMON + SEMF: --round1 on --tune on --pick base,d85 --round2 on --round3 on --r3-perq on --ans on --max-commits 300 --max-seeds 5 --boot 1000 --sem on --sem-model bge-small --engine-parity on), on a `git archive` copy of glia@9837b1ff with a copy of its sem cache, stderr timestamped and CPU sampled every 0.5 s (probe-f4o/rg/glia-run.{err,cpu}); load avg 8-25 from other agents during the run. Wall 533.7 s (`[rank_eval] glia: done in 533.7s`; the gate logs read 478 / 475 / 516 / 508 / 511 s at W20 / W21 / W25 / W26 / W27). Phases and mean cores: build 0-3 s; round1 + round2 3-24 s at 1.87 cores (`[round2] id routing for 300 test commits in 19.6s`); replay setup 24-31 s at 1.02; CALIBRATION 31-157 s at 1.62 cores (`[calibrate] text builds=300 docs_max=954 messages=yes ms=30282.3`, `[idr] replay surface=calibrate sides=297 routed=300 resolved=247 unavailable=0 ms=83372.7`, `[rank_eval] ans calibration sets=13 test_commits=300 ms=131191`); the evaluation 157-339 s at 12.88 cores (stats.eval_s 179.8); round3 339-396 s at 12.16 (`[round3] gates and 989 transfer queries in 57.0s`); engine parity 396-432 s at 12.32 (`done in 35.5s`); ans intent 432-522 s at 11.95 (`ms=89834`); tail 522-534 s at 0.99. So the PPR-heavy phases (eval, round3, parity, intent: 365 s) already run on ~12-13 of 16 cores (rank_eval's par_iter over queries; ANS CPU sum `[rank_eval] ans rankers=6 .. ms=2389562`). The one-core part is ~166 s (31%), and its largest block is the calibration replay, whose time is NOT PPR: IDR replay 83.4 s + text index rebuilds 30.3 s = 113.7 of 131.2 s. Read at HEAD: engine/src/calibrate/select.rs run_sets walks test commits in order and pools only one commit's ~4-6 queries (par_map_ordered over `qs`); TextState::begin_test_commit (fusions.rs) rebuilds TextIndex::from_docs over every earlier commit per test commit (300 builds, O(n^2)); IdrState computes its route lazily under a Mutex on the first query of a commit, so 300 parent-tree reads run one at a time. Both depend only on a prefix of the commit stream and the commit's parent tree, never on the online state, so they can be computed up front in order-preserving parallel maps. Also the shipped `glia history calibrate` runs this same replay, so the user-facing command speeds up too.

packets.implementation: The online loop stays sequential (state.observe(c) then begin_test_commit(k)); only work that depends on nothing the loop mutates moves ahead of it. (1) Text: the docs a test commit's TextIndex sees are a prefix of the commit stream (TextState::observe pushes in order), so compute every test commit's prefix length first, then build each `TextIndex::from_docs(prefix).scores(subject)` in par_map_ordered; begin_test_commit takes the precomputed vector. (2) IDR: each test commit's route reads its own parent tree, its subject and the older subjects (again a prefix): precompute in par_map_ordered, replacing the lazy Mutex. (3) Structure: P1 / PT* PPR vectors depend only on a query's seed nodes, never on co-change state: solve every query's vectors for all test commits in one par_map_ordered pass over a shared PprIndex (memo keyed by seed set), then score in the loop. Each solve keeps its own float order; results are collected in input order, so every vector is the same bits as now. Memory: the precomputed text scores are n_test x n_files f64 (300 x 2549 x 8 = 6 MB on glia), cap at a configurable chunk of test commits if a repo is larger. `[calibrate] text builds=` and `[idr] replay` gain ` threads=<t>`.

Mechanism, read at HEAD: DOCUMENTS is in CODE_TABLES.carry_edges (code-domain/src/profile.rs), .md is in rank::files NOT_CODE_EXTS so no doc is a candidate, and ANS:impact scores diff_impact's ROWS (rank_eval ans_keys_seed), which only the carry walk reaches: a doc section bound to many symbols was a hub joining code files that co-change, and FD.79 removed most of those hubs. File docs have no DOC_SPACE (engine/src/docs.rs emits one only for an external container); a repo file's DOC_SECTIONs carry its POSITION file. packets.title: Dockerfile image identity: FROM flags, multi-stage stages, and a generic build-context directory
packets.rationale: Two defects the start binding would inherit. (a) dockerfile_from_base (iac.rs:157) takes the first token after FROM, so `FROM --platform=$BUILDPLATFORM golang:..` mints `infra:image:--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM`; it reads only the FIRST FROM, so a multi-stage file's runtime base (distroless, alpine) is never read and `FROM base AS builder` would name a stage as an image. (b) dockerfile_image_name (iac.rs:136) names the image after the Dockerfile's parent directory, so src/cartservice/src/Dockerfile is `infra:image:src` and never joins `infra:deployment:cartservice -> infra:image:cartservice`. Probe at HEAD on microservices-demo (38e7348e): image nodes include `infra:image:--platform=$BUILDPLATFORM` (INFRA_REFERENCES from checkoutservice, currencyservice, emailservice, ...) and `infra:image:src`; INFRA_REFERENCES rows for cart: only `infra:deployment:cartservice -> infra:image:cartservice` (no Dockerfile behind it). skaffold.yaml:42-43 declares `image: cartservice` / `context: src/cartservice/src`.
entry_points: glia_code_extractors::iac::extract_dockerfile
glia_code_extractors::iac::extract_yaml
packets.implementation: Read every FROM: skip `--flag=value` tokens, record `AS <stage>`; a FROM naming an earlier stage is a stage parent, not an image (no INFRA_RESOURCE). The image's INFRA_REFERENCES base edges go to each external base the stages use (the final stage's base included). Image name: a build context declared by a compose `build:` (context / dockerfile), a skaffold `build.artifacts[] {image, context, docker.dockerfile}` in the same repo, else the parent directory, walking up past a generic name (src, app, docker, build, deploy, .docker, dockerfiles) to the first non-generic one. The declared-context lookup needs the compose / skaffold files, so it runs as a post-cache graft keyed like DT.10g's joins (engine/src/build/grafts.rs) or, simpler, in resolver:host when it re-keys: pick one and keep qnames stable across a watch update.

packets.area: the start rules of NEW.envhost.6; a package.json `scripts` reader (none exists at HEAD: no extractor reads `scripts`); a `.sh` reader for start-named scripts only
packets.rationale: Most real starts go through one hop the direct reader cannot see. twenty (cohort): docker-compose.yml:69 `["yarn", "worker:prod"]` -> packages/twenty-server/package.json:11 `"worker:prod": "node dist/queue-worker/queue-worker"` -> src/queue-worker/queue-worker.ts (tsconfig.json:16 `outDir: ./dist`); twenty Dockerfile:168-169 `CMD ["node", "dist/main"]` + `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]` whose last line is `exec "$@"` -> src/main.ts. plane (cohort): docker-compose.yml:60 `./bin/docker-entrypoint-worker.sh` whose last line is `celery -A plane worker -l info`; docker-entrypoint-api.sh ends `exec gunicorn .. plane.asgi:application`. mealie (cohort): docker/Dockerfile:167-170 copies docker/entry.sh to run.sh and ENTRYPOINTs it; entry.sh:95 `exec mealie` -> pyproject.toml:52 `mealie = "mealie.main:main"`. hoppscotch packages/hoppscotch-backend/Dockerfile:35 `pnpm run start:prod`. At HEAD none of these hops is read (no start reader exists, see NEW.envhost.3's probe).
entry_points: the start rules' PkgScript / Shell / Script(.sh) dispatch
packets.implementation: PkgScript: the package.json in the start's working dir (mapped through COPY) -> scripts[name] -> re-split, depth <= 3 (a script calling `npm run x` recurses; `pre<name>` scripts ignored). node <path> with a dist-like prefix: the nearest tsconfig*.json's compilerOptions.outDir maps to rootDir (else `src`), trying .ts / .tsx / .js / .mjs and `/index.*` (DERIVED). Shell script target (`*.sh`, or an extensionless file whose first line is a `#!` naming sh / bash): read its lines with the code_guard-free line scanner (the script is not code glia parses), take the `exec <cmd>` lines and, when none, the last simple command; `exec "$@"` / `exec $@` hands the start's remaining argv (the image CMD) through; the script's own MODULE does not exist (no shell parser), so the edge goes to the final target with rule `<host>:via_script` and the script path in the EVIDENCE detail. Console scripts reached by name (`exec mealie`) pair through NEW.envhost.3's CLI_INVOCATION and NEW.envhost.9's manifest binding.

packets.title: TSX / JSX files parse with tree-sitter's TSX grammar: the TS parser hard-codes LANGUAGE_TYPESCRIPT for every file, so a .tsx / .jsx / .js file's JSX is a syntax error, error recovery drops or hoists its declarations, and a React component ends as an edgeless, unlocated COMPONENT marker (or no node at all)
packets.rationale:
Found re-verifying FD.40 (GD.11, TS value positions). Cause, read at HEAD: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs parse_file_stats (~73) sets `tree_sitter_typescript::LANGUAGE_TYPESCRIPT` for every file; LANGUAGE_TSX is used nowhere in the workspace (`git grep LANGUAGE_TSX` empty) and no TS-parser code reads a jsx_* node. The plain TypeScript grammar has no JSX, so `` is parsed as type-assertion / comparison soup and error recovery decides what survives. There is no separate React parse path: engine/src/extract.rs detect_language maps tsx / jsx / js to "typescript" (only `.component.ts` -> angular), so the `"react"` arm of parse_one_as and glia_parser_react::parse_file / is_react_file are unreachable; the React extractor (parsers/code/extractors/src/react.rs scan_component_names, a line scan) runs for every TS file and mints COMPONENT / HOOK overlays with no cells, which LB.3a's fold (graph/src/roles.rs fold_role_overlays) merges into a same-qname FUNCTION when the parser minted one and otherwise leaves standalone. GD.11's rationale ('a file the React parser takes (`import React from 'react'`)') names the wrong trigger: the trigger is JSX the TS grammar's recovery cannot absorb, React import or not. Probes at HEAD with target/release/glia (glia 0.5.5 (build 0.5.5+p1aa31748d5678ab4), rebuilt 20:54 / 21:15 after every W0 code commit): (1) a tiny tree (probe-w0f/react1, react2: src/Btn.tsx `export function Btn() { return
; }` + src/Child.tsx `export const Child = () => { return child; };`, with and without `import React`): both build `FUNCTION 4, MODULE 2; DEFINES 4, CALLS 1, IMPORTS 1` - no USES Btn->handle, no edge Btn->Child, in either. (2) twenty's own files copied alone (probe-w0f/react3: EmailField.tsx + AiChatThreadRow.tsx from packages/twenty-front/src/modules/...): nodes `FUNCTION src::EmailField::handleStartEditing / handleCancelEditing / handleSave` (three locals of the component body hoisted to module level), `COMPONENT src::EmailField::EmailField ['COMPONENT']` (the marker, no FUNCTION), and for AiChatThreadRow.tsx only `INTERFACE ..AiChatThreadRowProps` and `FUNCTION ..stopPropagation`: the component `export const AiChatThreadRow = ({` (line 130) has no node at all. Bisect on EmailField.tsx: replacing the one JSX attribute `instanceId={`user-email-${currentUserId}`}` with a plain string makes the parser mint `FUNCTION EmailField` and drop the hoisted locals, i.e. recovery-dependent; minimal JSX files parse 'correctly' by luck. (3) twenty @8fd53a83 (cohort, git-archive copy probe-w0f/twenty, `glia build`): `[roles] folded 4859 overlays into declarations (COMPONENT=1489 HOOK=1026 SERVICE=1313 DIRECTIVE=0 PIPE=0 GUARD=5 COMPOSABLE=1026) standalone=1202`; `glia find e --kind COMPONENT --top-k 0 --json` -> 1172 COMPONENT rows, every one `file: null`, in-edges only (USES 404 bound by name to the marker, HANDLED_BY 1, DOCUMENTS 5), no out-edge. A regex survey of the 5,895 .tsx / .jsx files (top-level capitalised `function X` / `const X = (..` / `= async (` declarations, merge JSON of the same build): 2,936 have a FUNCTION node, 946 only a role marker (no POSITION, no edge), 970 no node at all; 1,760 files hold at least one such miss. twenty is 22,860 `={ident}` handler sites in .tsx / .jsx. The TSX grammar is tree-sitter-typescript 0.23's own second language (already in Cargo.lock): no dependency move. Needs a build probe to confirm the counts after (no cargo here).
entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs parse_file_stats (~66-80): pick the grammar from `file_rel_path`'s extension: `.tsx`, `.jsx`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs` -> LANGUAGE_TSX; `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts` and every other path (a Vue / Svelte / Astro script block the vue crate hands over with its own path, an Angular `.component.ts`) -> LANGUAGE_TYPESCRIPT, unchanged. ASCII-case-insensitive.

` only when n > 0 (one line per broken file, so a clean repo prints nothing)
parsers/code/react/src/lib.rs: delete the dead `is_react_file` (no caller) and say in the crate doc that the engine never routes a file to `react` (TS parse with the TSX grammar is the React parse)
packets.implementation: 1. Grammar by extension, as above; nothing else in the parser changes in this packet (the JSX reading is NEW.w0f.2). The TSX grammar is the TypeScript grammar plus JSX minus `<T>expr` angle-bracket assertions, which TS forbids in .tsx anyway, and which no .js / .jsx file can hold; generic arrows in .tsx are written `<T,>(..)` by their authors already. 2. Unit tests in the parser: a twenty-shaped component (an arrow component with locals, a JSX attribute holding a template literal, a JSX ternary) parses with zero error nodes and mints exactly one top-level FUNCTION for the component and none for its locals; the same text in a `.ts` path keeps today's TYPESCRIPT grammar; a `.js` file with JSX parses clean; a `.ts` file with `<T>x` assertions parses clean (TYPESCRIPT kept). 3. Fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/react-tsx-components: src/EmailField.tsx (the bisected shape, trimmed), src/Row.tsx (a multi-line `export const Row = ({ a, b }: Props) => {` component), src/Child.tsx; key: expect_nodes FUNCTION EmailField, FUNCTION Row, FUNCTION Child; expect_cells ROLE contains COMPONENT on EmailField and Child (the line-scanner still supplies the role where it fires); forbid FUNCTION handleSave at module level (spelled as grade.py --dump spells it at the base) and forbid a standalone COMPONENT EmailField. 4. PARSER_STAMP moves (parsers). Record twenty's before / after numbers in the commit body.

packets.title: JSX is read: a `<Child />` / `<Ns.Child>` element is a USES of the component it names, a JSX attribute expression (`onClick={handle}`, `render={Row}`) is a value position, and a capitalised function or arrow whose body returns JSX gets ROLE COMPONENT from the AST, replacing react.rs's line scan for components

NEW.w0f.1 makes JSX parse; nothing reads it yet: `git grep -n 'jsx_' -- parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs` is empty at HEAD, so even in a file the TS grammar happens to recover, a JSX element or attribute binds nothing. Probe at HEAD (target/release/glia (glia 0.5.5 (build 0.5.5+p1aa31748d5678ab4), rebuilt 20:54 / 21:15 after every W0 code commit), probe-w0f/react1 and react2, src/Btn.tsx `return

On twenty @8fd53a83 (cohort): packages/twenty-front/src/modules/ai/components/AiChatThreadRow.tsx:217-218 and 229-230 `onClick={stopPropagation} onContextMenu={stopPropagation}` -> `[ts-value-refs] refs=0 in_file=0 imported=0 const_inits=11 .. file=..AiChatThreadRow.tsx` and FUNCTION `..AiChatThreadRow::stopPropagation` `live: False`; repo-wide 3,761 `on={ident}` sites and ~22.9k `` on the declaration's first line, so a multi-line arrow component (`export const AiChatThreadRow = ({` .. `}) => {`, AiChatThreadRow.tsx:130) gets no ROLE even once NEW.w0f.1 mints its FUNCTION.
entry_points: parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs: the value-ref walk (DT.5g, `value_ref` emission ~7990) gains JSX positions: `jsx_opening_element` / `jsx_self_closing_element` name (an identifier starting uppercase, or a `member_expression` `Ns.Comp` read as its leftmost identifier through the namespace import) -> a value ref from the enclosing callable (in-file FUNCTION / CLASS / STATE_VAR -> USES rule `jsx_element`; an imported name -> the Bare USES ref the graph binds through the named / default import, rule `jsx_element`); lowercase intrinsic tags (`div`) and `<this.X>` read nothing. A `jsx_expression` attribute value or child that is a bare identifier or a `member_expression` on `this` is a value ref (rule `jsx_attribute`), the DT.5g walk's rules otherwise (calls inside `{..}` are already calls once the tree parses).

packets.title: Include-style route mounts, the mechanism and Django: a route file mounted under a prefix BY REFERENCE to its module (`path("api/", include("plane.app.urls"))`, nested includes, a urlpatterns list imported by name and spread) gives each of its routes the full path `/<prefix><path>`, through CB.20's mount fixpoint generalised with a module slot; Django routes gain their POSITION and the include() line stops minting a ROUTE
packets.area: HTTP routes / route mounts (James 2026-10-31: "yeah thats an annoying case to generalise")
packets.rationale: next-leap-0.5.6.md §7 lists it. Probe at HEAD (target/release/glia (glia 0.5.5 (build 0.5.5+p1aa31748d5678ab4), rebuilt 20:54 / 21:15 after every W0 code commit), git-archive copy of cohort repo plane @d9726d5c under probe-w0f/plane, `glia build`): `[http] routes=384 endpoints=483 paired=0 (exact=0 any=0 eprefix=0 ..)`, `[http-qname] routes=384 endpoints=503 noncanonical=357 ..`, first three `["ANY admins/ @apps/api", "ANY admins/<uuid:pk>/ @apps/api", "ANY admins/me/ @apps/api"]` (GD.26 landed: `[http-wrappers] .. heritage_minted=470`, so plane's client side now exists and the server side is what is missing). `glia find <plane> / --kind ROUTE --top-k 0 --json`: 357 of 384 ROUTEs have `file: null`. Cause, read at HEAD: parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs scan_django_routes (~3358) emits every `path` / `re_path` / `url` call's first string literal through emit_route_no_handler as `ANY <literal>`: no POSITION, no leading `/`, no module, the include() prefix lost, and `path("api/", include(..))` itself minted as a ROUTE `ANY api/`. plane: apps/api/plane/urls.py:19-24 `path("api/", include("plane.app.urls"))`, `api/public/` -> plane.space.urls, `api/instances/` -> plane.license.urls, `api/v1/` -> plane.api.urls, `auth/` -> plane.authentication.urls, `""` -> plane.web.urls; apps/api/plane/app/urls/__init__.py imports `from .issue import urlpatterns as issue_urls` (20 such) and lists `*issue_urls`. A simulation of the fold over plane's url modules (probe-w0f/djsim.py: literal includes and spread imports only) gives 380 routes, and 378 of plane's 477 non-test ENDPOINTs match a folded route path exactly (the rest: `/api/..` endpoints of views no urlconf lists, `<unresolved>` 19). Tiny-tree probe (probe-w0f/mounts/dj: proj/urls.py include of app.urls and app.auth_urls, app/urls/__init__.py spreading `from .issue import urlpatterns as issue_urls` and including app.urls.nested): `[http] routes=6 endpoints=3 paired=0`, ROUTEs `ANY v2/`, `ANY api/`, `ANY auth/`, `ANY login/`, `ANY things/`, `ANY workspaces/<str:slug>/issues/`, every one `file: None`. What glia already folds (same probes, mounts/*): Go groups across files (CB.20 graph/src/go_mounts.rs: `api.Register(r.Group("/svc/v9"))` -> `GET /svc/v9/things` internal/api/routes.go:4, paired exact); Rails `namespace :api` / `scope '/v9'` in routes.rb (`ANY /api/users`, `GET /v9/things`); Flask `Blueprint(url_prefix=)` and FastAPI `APIRouter(prefix=)` + same-file `include_router(prefix=)` (scan_router_prefixes ~3149, whose doc says cross-file include_router is 'deliberately OUT of scope'); NestJS `@Controller(prefix)`. Not folded: Django include(), Flask `register_blueprint(bp, url_prefix=)` across files (`GET /items` bp.py:4), FastAPI cross-file `include_router(users.router, prefix="/api")` (`GET /users`), Express `app.use('/api/users', require('./routes/users'))` and `app.use('/api/items', items)` (`GET /list`, `GET /all`, paired=0), even same-file `app.use('/zz/users', router)` (`GET /list`), NestJS `setGlobalPrefix('svc')` and `RouterModule.register([{ path: 'backoffice', module: AdminModule }])` (`GET /users/all`, paired=0). The Flask / FastAPI probes pair only because `api` is in the resolver's default strip list (graph/src/resolvers/http.rs API_PREFIXES, tier eprefix). This packet builds the mechanism with Django on it; NEW.w0f.4 (Python) and NEW.w0f.5 (TS) put the other shapes on the same facts.
entry_points: code-domain/src/lib.rs: `Mount::Module { module: String, var: String, suffix: String }` (a route registered on router value `var` of MODULE `module`; `var` = `urlpatterns` for Django) and `NavFact::IncludeMount { line: u32, target: IncludeTarget, prefix: String, via: String }` with `IncludeTarget::Spec(String)` (a dotted module path / relative specifier as written) and `IncludeTarget::Import { local: String }` (a name the file imports), both appended at the END of their enums (bincode tags); `endpoint::mount_route_qname` / `parse_mount_route_qname` learn `<mount:module:<module>#<var>>`

parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs scan_django_routes: a `path` / `re_path` / `url` call in a module that holds `urlpatterns` is minted under the provisional `ANY <mount:module:<module qname>#urlpatterns><literal>` with a POSITION cell at the call row; `include("<dotted>")` records IncludeMount{Spec} and mints no ROUTE; `*name` inside the urlpatterns list (or `urlpatterns += name`) where `name` is imported as `from <m> import urlpatterns as name` records IncludeMount{Import, prefix ""}; `include(<non-literal>)` (DRF `router.urls`, a variable) is counted `dynamic` and mints nothing

graph/src/build/route_mounts.rs (new child module of build.rs, like build/go_wire.rs): `bind_module_mounts(g, refs, lang)` - resolves each IncludeMount's target to a MODULE (Spec: a dotted path matched to a file MODULE by qname tail, `pkg` -> `pkg::__init__`; Import: the importing file's IMPORTS binding of `local`), runs CB.20's fixpoint over module slots (a slot's prefixes = each includer's own prefixes joined with the include literal; cycles and > 32 prefixes stop as in go_mounts), then re-keys each provisional ROUTE to `<METHOD> /<prefix><path>` once per prefix, an unmounted one to `<METHOD> /<path>`
graph/src/go_mounts.rs: factor the provisional-ROUTE re-key (rename_nodes for the first prefix, clone_route ~599 for each further one, refs carried) into one fn both passes call
graph/src/build.rs: `mod route_mounts;` and the call in build_python after resolve_imports_python and resolve_calls, before resolve_refs (where build_go_passes calls go_mounts::bind)

packets.area: T8 / watch latency (agreed follow-up of GA.20)
packets.rationale: GA.20 (17e5cfb8) timed every graft and memoized the A16.4 IMPORTS filter, and its body says the halving was NOT met: 'the two steps left on top are the wrapper inference (external::infer_entity_wrappers: per HTTP family a direct_http pass over every file, then a forwarding pass scanning every file per frontier call) and the wrapper call-site scan (external::WrapperPass::scan: every stanza's call text searched in every file before scan_file) .. their files belong to GD.26 this wave.' GD.26 (72605887) has landed and added heritage_scopes (every TS CLASS of every file, per build) and scan_heritage. Probe at HEAD (target/release/glia (glia 0.5.5 (build 0.5.5+p1aa31748d5678ab4), rebuilt 20:54 / 21:15 after every W0 code commit), git-archive copies of the cohort pins under probe-w0f, `glia watch <copy> --persist-every 0 --poll-ms 100 --debounce-ms 100`, one comment line appended per update, probe-w0f/watchprobe.sh): twenty @8fd53a83 per update `[timing] grafts repo=twenty modules=52.9ms infer_wrappers=389.9ms wrapper_scan=134.2ms wrappers_http=9.6ms evm_abi=31.1ms endpoint_fold=50.1ms .. owner=55.6ms .. imports_filter=100.1ms` (infer_wrappers 350-394, wrapper_scan 131-141 over 3 updates), phase_ms.grafts 963 / 1,031 / 1,048; prefect @fa93ba25 `infer_wrappers=550.5ms wrapper_scan=308.5ms .. imports_filter=21.0ms` (519-551 and 305-319 over 4 updates), phase_ms.grafts 908 / 936 / 937 / 949, with `[graft-memo] const hit=3686/3687 .. imports hit=3687/3687 index=hit repo=prefect` and `[http-wrappers] wrappers=75 sites=19 ..`. Every other step sums to ~520 ms on twenty and ~100 ms on prefect, so the wrapper pair is what stands between today and GA.20's target. Code read at HEAD: engine/src/external/infer_wrappers.rs infer_http (~842: per family, catch_unwind(direct_http(f)) for every file, then per depth `for (call, shape) in frontier { for f in code.filter(|f| f.source.contains(call)) }`), infer_collections (~330, the Go twin with direct_candidates / forwarding_candidates), heritage_scopes (~1936); engine/src/external/wrappers.rs WrapperPass::scan (~558: per file `pass.stanzas.iter().any(|s| .. source.contains(s.decl.call))` then scan_file + scan_heritage). direct_http reads only its own CodeFile (path, source, lang, parse) and returns strings (HttpCandidate: call, shape, def_file, def_line0, via, class), so its output is a pure per-file value.
entry_points: engine/src/build/memo.rs: `WrapperMemo` (one entry per walked path): key `WrapperKey { lang, source digest (xxh3-128 of the text), module qname }` -> the file's DirectHttp (cands, unparsed, gate) per HTTP family, its Go direct candidates, its heritage ClassFile record (classes, spans, bases, imports) and its needle hits (below); and `ScanMemo`: key (WrapperKey, stanza-set digest, the file's heritage-scope digest) -> the file's sites and ambiguous count; the module doc's CONTRACT gains both

engine/src/external/infer_wrappers.rs: infer_http / infer_collections read the per-file outputs from the memo and compute only misses (on the pool, folded in walk order, as DC.4's memos do); the forwarding loop runs one pass per file per depth over the frontier's call texts (exact `str::contains` semantics per call, so the hit set is the same set of (file, call) pairs), hits memoized per (WrapperKey, call) so an unchanged file answers from the memo; heritage_scopes joins memoized per-file class records
engine/src/external/wrappers.rs WrapperPass::scan: the per-file stanza gate and scan_file / scan_heritage output replayed from ScanMemo on a hit
engine/src/build/grafts.rs apply_post_cache: hands `memo` to the two stages (it already holds it for the imports filter); `[graft-memo]` gains ` wrappers hit=<h>/<n> scan hit=<h>/<n>` before ` repo=`

The two memos and their keys, documented in memo.rs's CONTRACT (a later packet that gives direct_http, the forwarding reader or scan_file a new input adds it to the key in the same commit). 2. Misses computed on the engine pool, inserts in the sequential fold, hits cloned: byte-identical by construction. 3. The forwarding needle pass: per depth, each file is visited once and tested against every frontier call; no new crate (aho-corasick is in Cargo.lock only transitively; adding it as a direct dependency moves engine/Cargo.toml and is not needed for the target). 4. watch_parity: scripted cases - an edit that creates a wrapper (a new direct candidate in the edited file: every caller elsewhere must mint), an edit that adds a call site of an existing wrapper, an edit that removes a heritage base, a rename that moves a file's module qname (the key must miss); each falsified by dropping one key part. 5. GB.3's correction left the question open ('no gate measured node-to-flow matching'). James asked to keep or remove it by a gate. Precedent: FB.6 (the semantic tier alone, FAIL, never shipped) and FB.6b (the blend, PASS, shipped). This packet is the same shape for flows: a rule committed before the numbers, held-out commits, a paired bootstrap against controls that isolate the similarity's share.

packets.implementation:
1. Write dev-notes/concept-gate-0.5.6.md's rule section FIRST and commit it before any panel run (the commit is the rule's timestamp; the report quotes its sha). THE CONCEPT RULE: Panel = the nine `verdict` rows of bench/rank-gate/fusion-preview.json at their pinned revs and windows (FB.6b's; the forward windows of commons-lang / commons-io via `--test-after`), reusing $GLIA_RANK_GATE_DIR/sem's cached bge-small vectors. GB.3's configuration is fixed and never tuned here (it was never run on these repos for flows). Query set per repo: the test window's commits whose subject (redacted as EB.1 stores it) makes GB.1's lexical `concept_flows` (semantic None) return NO row: the only queries where the tier fires. Truth per query: the head build's entry flows (`entry_flows`, the depth / limit GB.3's CLI default uses) with at least one hop located in a file the commit changed (the find shape's truth files). A query with no truth flow is dropped and counted. Rankers, each returning a flow order truncated at k: S = GB.3's semantic tier exactly (`concept_flows` with the SemanticSource and a RankCache, the shipped call); Clex = the same flow mapping fed by LX[IDR,T1s] (find --files with `semantic: None`: every step of S except the similarity); Creach = all flows by reach desc, then key (no query); Crand = a seeded random flow order (information only). Metric: flow hit@5 (any of the first 5 rows is a truth flow); precision@5 and hit@1 are information rows. Every a - b is `--gate-pair`'s paired commit-cluster bootstrap 95% CI (B = 1000) on that repo's concept queries. A repo with fewer than 30 concept queries is reported and left out; n = the repos left. RULE: C1 = S - Clex has CI lo > 0 on >= ceil(n/2) repos and CI hi >= 0 on all n; C2 = S - Creach has CI lo > 0 on >= ceil(n/2) repos and CI hi >= 0 on all n. PASS = C1 and C2 with n >= 5; n < 5 is INSUFFICIENT and reads as FAIL. ON PASS nothing in the answers changes and GZ.1 cites the report. ON FAIL (James 2026-11-01: "Nah concept search can be put to backlog if it fails") the tier goes to the backlog, not away for good: the integrator writes the packet that takes it out of 0.5.6 (ConceptTier::Semantic, ConceptHit.similarity, ConceptOptions / TraceOptions.{semantic, rank_cache}, resolved_by `concept_semantic`, `flows` / `trace --no-semantic` and `concept_flows(semantic=)`; concept search is lexical only, GB.1's answer byte for byte; the GZ.2 handoff entry from GB.3 is withdrawn) and adds a dev-notes/precision-backlog.json entry naming this report, GB.3's commits (aec37667, 9bb8ca3d) and the rule rows it missed, so a later release can retry it.
2. rank_eval: `--concept on` after every existing row (no existing row, key or JSON field moves without the flag; the existing `--sem on` find rows are untouched). Build the head graph once per repo (it already does for `--engine`), compute entry_flows once, a per-flow file set, and per query the four orders. JSON gains `concept { queries, dropped_no_truth, lexical_hit_queries, rows: [{ranker, hit1, hit5, p5}], per_query: [{sha, s, clex, creach, crand}] }`; `--gate-pair "S,Clex;S,Creach" --gate-shape concept` reads per_query hit5. fired_on: `[concept-eval] label=<l> test=<t> lexical_hit=<h> concept_queries=<q> dropped_no_truth=<d> flows=<f> ms=<ms>` once per repo and `[rank-gate] pair label=<l> shape=concept a=<a> b=<b> metric=hit5 diff=.. ci=[..]` per pair.
3. scripts/embedding-gate.sh `concept-verdict` (build rank_eval with --features sem-eval as fusion-verdict does, run the nine with `--sem on --concept on`, judge) and `concept-verdict-judge` (re-judge only). The judge prints per repo n / pairs, then `CONCEPT: C1=<yes|no> (<k>/<n>) C2=<yes|no> (<k>/<n>) -> PASS|FAIL|INSUFFICIENT`, and appends the tables and `VERDICT: <v>` to the report under its `<!-- concept-gate:verdict -->` anchor.
4. Every number in the report is an aggregate over a public repository (the repo is public).

packets.acceptance:
(1) The rule section is committed before any panel run; the report names that commit. (2) `cargo build --release -p glia-engine --example rank_eval --features sem-eval` green; without `--concept on` a run of one panel repo writes byte-identical JSON to HEAD's binary (diff of the two --out files, recorded in the commit body). (3) `bash scripts/embedding-gate.sh concept-verdict` ends `VERDICT: PASS`, `FAIL` or `INSUFFICIENT`, and the report holds per repo: test commits, lexical-hit queries, concept queries, dropped (no truth), flows, and every rule and information row with its CI. (4) `cargo test -p glia-engine --test engine_tests` green. (5) CLOSE-OUT (not the wave agent): the rank gate's run reads byte-identical rows (rank_eval's existing rows unmoved).

packets.title: Start indirection, the shell half: the exec / last command of the entry scripts a start names (never every .sh), `exec "$@"` passthrough, plus tsconfig outDir / rootDir for dist -> src
packets.area: the start rules of GH.18 / GH.19 (graph/src/resolvers/host_start.rs resolve_launch); a build-time read of the shell scripts a start cell's argv names
packets.rationale: GH.19 (9679d051) built the package-manager-script and dist -> src hops but reported partial: the build holds no `.sh` text (the walk admits no .sh and no extensionless shebang file; route.rs sees only walked (path, source) pairs and has no repo root; RepoBuildCtx carries none), and reading the scripts a start names needs engine/src/build/assemble.rs + build/mod.rs plumbing it did not own. Probe at HEAD c452b1e8 (GH.19's own run): plane apps/api prints `[host-start] .. scripts_unread=10`. The cohort shapes from GH.19's rationale stay unread: twenty Dockerfile `ENTRYPOINT ["/app/entrypoint.sh"]` ending `exec "$@"` + `CMD ["node", "dist/main"]` -> src/main.ts; plane docker-entrypoint-worker.sh ending `celery -A plane worker -l info`, docker-entrypoint-api.sh ending `exec gunicorn .. plane.asgi:application`; mealie docker/entry.sh:95 `exec mealie` -> pyproject.toml:52 `mealie = "mealie.main:main"`. GH.19's tsconfig follow-up rides here (its cross-env LAUNCHERS row goes to GH.10, which owns code-domain/src/hosts.rs): dist -> src maps only the dist/build/out/lib -> src convention because the walk keeps no tsconfig `compilerOptions.outDir` / `rootDir` / `extends`.
entry_points: engine/src/build/assemble.rs parse_and_graft (repo root in hand): after routing, collect the start cells' argv script targets (a path-shaped argv[0], or the script a `sh` / `bash` / `/bin/sh -c` launcher runs) mapped through each image's COPY map / the declaring file's dir, and read each named file from disk
parsers/code/extractors/src/iac.rs: the entry-script reader (exec lines, else the last simple command)
graph/src/resolvers/host_start.rs resolve_launch: the shell / passthrough hops
engine/src/walk.rs: keep tsconfig outDir / rootDir / extends per project dir
packets.implementation:
1. Script read (assemble.rs + build/mod.rs): after routing, with the repo root, gather every start cell's script target (argv[0] path-shaped, or the script argument of a shell launcher), resolved through the image's COPY map (GH.18's) else relative to the cell's workdir / dir. Read only those files, at most 4 KiB each, at most 64 per repo, never by extension and never every .sh (the James rule: shell entry scripts are read for their start / exec line only). A script that is missing, binary or over the cap is counted `scripts_unread`. 2. Reader (iac.rs): keep the `exec ` lines; with none, the last simple command (skip comments, blank lines, `set` / `export` / `cd` / `fi` / `done`, function bodies); never anything else. Record the kept line(s) as a CODE cell on the script's start target the host_start resolver reads (`{"script":,"exec":,"row":<1-based>}`); the script's other text is not stored. 3. Hops (host_start.rs resolve_launch): `shell` follows the script's kept command as the start's argv (rule `:via_script`, the script path in the evidence); `passthrough` reads `exec "$@"` (normalise_argv returns Binary `$@`, refused dynamic today, chain [.., exec]) as the remaining argv: the image CMD / compose command. A script calling a script counts toward GH.19's 3-hop limit. `exec mealie` mints cli_invoke:mealie from the Dockerfile MODULE via crate::cli::argv_cell (GH.15's handoff), binding the console-script entry. 4. tsconfig (walk.rs): keep compilerOptions.outDir / rootDir (following `extends`) per project dir, and dist -> src maps those declared dirs first, the convention only when none is declared. 5. coverage.rs: update the (host, HANDLED_BY) caveat: package-manager scripts (<= 3 hops), compiled dist paths (derived) and the exec line of start-named entry scripts are read; any other shell is not. Regenerate the reflexion golden with GLIA_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p glia-engine --lib rules::reflexion_parity and declare it as a cli_output break. 6. Marker: extend `[host-start] hops=(pkg_script=

dist_src=)` to `hops=(pkg_script=

dist_src= shell= passthrough=) refused_depth= scripts_unread=`.
